title: Settling an owned question is never past the objective
situation: Two of the architect's guards conflict over an owned open question: the past-objective guard refuses recording one the operator did not ask about, while the hand-back guard demands it be settled.
decision: Under 0090, settling and recording a meaning question the architect owns, when it holds what that needs, is part of its objective in any turn and never procedure past it. Whether it holds what the question needs is judged once, by one rule, and every guard reads that one judgment: holding it, the architect settles and records; lacking it, it reports the one action that will get it.
consequences: The past-objective and hand-back guards share that one judgment instead of each deciding it.
